title: Angular
note: AngularJS was the first framework I used, and I loved how easy it was to build interactive apps with two-way data binding. I adopted Angular 2+ immediately and still miss working with it sometimes.

title: Vue.js
note: This is my main stack — I've been working with Vue for close to 5 years now, and I'm still in love with it.

title: React
note: Not my personal favorite, but the most widely used framework out there for good reasons — a must-have in any developer's toolkit.

title: Astro
note: So far my favorite static site generator. I like how simple it is to build with, and it lets you mix multiple frameworks in the same project.

title: Tailwind CSS
note: My go-to CSS framework, once you get used to its philosophy — otherwise changing a style is a headache.

title: Vite
note: If you've ever worked with webpack, you know why I love Vite.

title: Vitest
note: A Vite-native testing framework. I used to skip unit tests because Jest always felt slow — with Vitest that's not an excuse anymore.

title: Nuxt
note: An incredible framework for building Vue apps. I spend most of my workdays in it — easy to start, with a lot more power underneath.

title: Qwik
note: Resumability lets you build extremely fast apps. If you know React, you already know about 80% of it.

title: Next.js
note: The first framework that introduced me to page-based routing on top of React. A lot of similarities with Nuxt.

title: Remix
note: Haven't had the chance to use it much yet, but it's on my watchlist.

title: RxJS
note: Takes real effort to wrap your mind around, but incredibly powerful and flexible once it clicks.
